name: Central Thimphu
tagline: Norzin Lam and the grid around it
description: The centre of the capital along Norzin Lam, with the shops, restaurants, the weekend market and the traffic junction where a policeman directs cars from a decorated booth because the city has no traffic lights. It is compact and walkable.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to be in the middle of the only real town in Bhutan
pros: The weekend market and the shops
cons: The most expensive accommodation in the city
Busy and dusty in the daytime

name: Tashichho Dzong and the North
tagline: The fortress-monastery and the government quarter
description: The northern end of the valley, where Tashichho Dzong houses both the government and the central monastic body, with the parliament, the royal residence and the more expensive housing on the slopes above. The riverside walk runs the whole way.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the dzong and the riverside walk on the doorstep
pros: Quieter and greener than the centre
cons: Twenty minutes from the shops on foot
Very little in the way of restaurants
Access to some areas is restricted

name: Motithang and the Western Slopes
tagline: Up the hill, with the takin preserve
description: The residential slopes on the western side of the valley above the centre, holding much of Thimphu's better housing, the takin preserve where Bhutan's odd national animal is kept, and the trailheads for the walks up to Tango and Cheri monasteries.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting quiet, air and a walk from the door
pros: Cooler, quieter and greener than the valley floor
The takin preserve and forest trails
cons: A steep walk or a taxi to the centre

name: Buddha Dordenma and the South
description: The southern end of the valley, dominated by the Buddha Dordenma, a fifty-one-metre gilded bronze statue on a hill above the city that is visible from most of Thimphu, with the newer southern housing and the road out towards Paro below it.
bestFor: Anyone wanting newer housing and the road to Paro
pros: The Buddha Dordenma and its viewpoint
Closest to the Paro road and the airport
cons: Character is suburban rather than Bhutanese
